units.unit: Needs peer-reviewed work measuring how binding rent ceilings affect supply of subdivided or informal rental stock
Wants a distinction between controls on rent levels versus controls on increases within a tenancy
The ordinance capped increases within a tenancy but left the initial rent untouched
That is why it is called second-generation
The instrument was never binding at the point that matters
The weakest claim is that a hard cap on initial rents would shrink the stock enough to shut out new households
Berlin shows this happening in practice
Needs the stock-elasticity paper with its first- vs second-generation distinction
